desc: Trace FDs passed through unix sockets. Uses Linux eBPF/bcc.
r: sofdsnoop - Trace FDs passed through unix sockets. Uses Linux eBPF/bcc.

sofdsnoop traces FDs passed through unix sockets

Every file descriptor that is passed via unix sockets os displayed on separate line together with process info (TID/COMM columns), ACTION details (SEND/RECV), file descriptor number (FD) and its translation to file if available (NAME).

Since this uses BPF, only the root user can use this tool.

<dl><dt data-o="">-h</dt><dd>Print usage message.</dd><dt data-o="">-T</dt><dd>Include a timestamp column.</dd><dt data-o="">-p PID</dt><dd>Trace this process ID only (filtered in-kernel).</dd><dt data-o="">-t TID</dt><dd>Trace this thread ID only (filtered in-kernel).</dd><dt data-o="">-d DURATION</dt><dd>Total duration of trace in seconds.</dd><dt data-o="">-n NAME</dt><dd>Only print command lines matching this command name (regex)</dd></dl>

Trace all sockets:
# sofdsnoop
Trace all sockets, and include timestamps:
# sofdsnoop -T
Only trace sockets where the process contains "server":
# sofdsnoop -n server

<dl><dt>TIME(s)</dt><dd>Time of SEDN/RECV actions, in seconds.</dd><dt>ACTION</dt><dd>Operation on the fd SEND/RECV.</dd><dt>TID</dt><dd>Process TID</dd><dt>COMM</dt><dd>Parent process/command name.</dd><dt>SOCKET</dt><dd>The socket carrier.</dd><dt>FD</dt><dd>file descriptor number</dd><dt>NAME</dt><dd>file name for SEND lines</dd></dl>

This is from bcc.

https://github.com/iovisor/bcc

Also look in the bcc distribution for a companion _examples.txt file containing example usage, output, and commentary for this tool.
